boundaryStatement: The nautilus_agents authority model (agents propose narrow semantic intents over engine-owned observations; the engine owns every production decision; agent processes hold no venue authority) confirms and does not change the QuantOS boundary: an Agent never connects to a venue directly. These rules keep it that way.

rules.rule: Agent processes must never hold venue credentials or invoke venue/exchange/order APIs, directly or through tools.
rules.enforcement: TP04 adapter rejects order/order_tool/trade_command/venue/secret/network fields; engine UDS boundary carries no venue material

rules.rule: Agent output may only be a TradeProposal with executable=false; any executable=true output is rejected.
rules.enforcement: TP04 proposal mapper hard-codes executable=False; R04 runtime gate rejects executable proposals

rules.rule: No TradeCommand may be issued from agent output without an authoritative RiskDecision (and approval when required); agent-side checks are advisory only.
rules.enforcement: quantos-execution CommandIssuer requires a RiskDecision and enforces the approval state machine

rules.rule: Execution kernels receive only sanitized BoundaryCommand values; tenant, actor, session, decision, approval, and signature material must never cross the kernel boundary.
rules.enforcement: TP07 ExecutionGateway sanitizes before kernel submit; isolation test enforces the key allowlist and forbidden terms

rules.rule: Agent-side traces and local evidence are advisory; production evidence must be recorded by the runtime/kernel artifact path, never by the agent process alone.
rules.enforcement: R03/R04 runtime records artifact manifests with content hashes; agent engine outputs only feed runtime records

rules.rule: Expired proposals must be 100% rejected before evaluation, issuance, and kernel submission.
rules.enforcement: R04 TradeProposalEvaluationGate at evaluation, X02 issuer proposal-expiry check, TP07 gateway CommandExpired rejection

rules.rule: The nautilus-agents crate (and any Nautilus-family code) must never enter a QuantOS lockfile or runtime dependency graph; collaboration happens at design/protocol level only.
rules.enforcement: TP12 baseline policy + TP07 LGPL ADR process-boundary decision
